posts.title: Established ‘TMNT’ Fans Will Appreciate Series’ Latest Story Arc And Its Presentation
posts.description: Courtesy: IDW Publishing IDW Publishing made a massive move with its Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles comics series in December 2019 when it killed off the Turtles’ father, Splinter, also known from his previous life as Hamato Yoshi. His death sent shockwaves through the TMNT comics universe as it ended up playing a huge role in the outcome of the series’ initial 150-issue run. Almost one year ago now, writer Gene Luen Yang brought Splinter back from the dead in Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles #13 . The debut issue for Yang, it “resurrected” Splinter as the seriously dangerous killer, “Ujigami.” Now the 6-part arc involving Splinter’s return to the land of the living is available in a brand-new collection dubbed Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles : Ujigami . Also going by the title Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles Volume 3 , this collection is another mostly positive entry from this latest run of the hit series. That is proven largely through its story. posts.title: Phil’s Picks Must-See Standalone Flicks #63 — ‘The Incredible Mr. Limpet’
posts.description: Courtesy: Warner Bros. Don Knotts is one of the most well-known and respected comedic actors in Hollywood’s modern history. That is thanks primarily to his work on the timeless CBS sitcom, The Andy Griffith Show . There is no doubt that after he and fellow cast mate Jim Nabors left the show, it really went downhill. The movies in which he starred have themselves largely come to be their own beloved works; all except maybe for one, The Incredible Mr. Limpet . Knotts’ first movie role while on hiatus from The Andy Griffith Show , this 1964 movie from Warner Bros. is unique from the rest of Knott’s cinematic work mainly because it was primarily voiceover work instead of on camera work. This, against the story, is really at the core of what makes it notable. While the movie itself honestly deserves more attention than it has gotten, its home release is not perfect. posts.title: Saturday Morning Fun Continues Again In New ‘TMNT’ Comics Collection
posts.description: Courtesy: IDW Publishing This past September, IDW Publishing wrapped its Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles : Saturday Morning Adventures comics series with the release of the series’ 41 st issue and next spring it will be brought together with Issues 37-40 in Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles : Saturday Morning Adventures Volume 10 . That collection is set for release March 9. That means in the meantime readers have more than enough time to catch up on everything that has been going on in the series. Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles : Saturday Morning Adventures Volume 9 , released Nov. 10, will do just that in its own right. Spanning Issues 32-36, the stories in those issues are at the heart of the collection. The general writing within the stories adds to the appeal in its own right, as does the art, once again.
